title: Harness engineering
supportingClaims: Keep repository instructions concise and put actionable knowledge, constraints, and evidence into the working repository.
limitations: Describes OpenAI's internal experience; its scale and infrastructure are not required for this repository.

title: HALAS: A Human-Annotated Dataset of Hallucinations of Modern ASR Systems
supportingClaims: ASR hallucinations can be evaluated with human span-level labels; ordinary WER alone does not describe all unsupported content.
limitations: External dataset results do not establish this product's Japanese Meet quality or M1 performance; no dataset audio was downloaded or reused.

title: SimulStreaming
supportingClaims: Streaming speech translation behavior and latency require an incremental evaluation path; request/response chunking alone is not proof of streaming inference.
limitations: No code or model from this project was integrated; no M1 compatibility claim is made.

title: SacreBLEU
supportingClaims: The implementation reports metric signatures and exposes chrF configuration such as character order, word order, beta, and whitespace handling.
limitations: The repository's internal ChrF-like score is not reported as SacreBLEU; no SacreBLEU package/version has been pinned or run here.

title: whisper.cpp decoder and segment emission
supportingClaims: At the pinned source revision, the decoder computes no-speech probability and combines it with average log probability to suppress segment text before returning it; the public API exposes segment timing and no-speech values, while the bridge can read token log probabilities.
limitations: The source behavior is Whisper-specific. A source commit does not pin downloaded Whisper weights, establish score calibration, or prove native Metal and end-to-end quality.

title: Qwen3-ASR-0.6B-hf (Transformers-native model card)
supportingClaims: The card lists Japanese and English among 30 supported languages; the family overview also counts 22 Chinese dialects.
The hosted 0.6B checkpoint metadata reports 0.8B parameters and BF16 weights; this differs from the model nickname.

The official processor exposes apply_transcription_request with an optional language name/code and vocabulary prompt. Its forced-language assistant prefix is `language <NAME><asr_text>` and decoded output supports parsed or transcription-only forms.

The official card states native Transformers support from v5.13.0. Word timestamps require the separate Qwen3-ForcedAligner model; the English example sets max_new_tokens=256 but does not define an EOS or calibrated confidence contract.
limitations: The official load examples use Transformers/PyTorch; they do not establish M1 Metal execution or performance. Community MLX-Audio lists a separate 0.6B 8-bit conversion, but its exact revision and output semantics are not locked here.
The model card reports other-corpus results, not Japanese Google Meet quality. Language metadata and an example template do not supply an EOS policy or calibrated publication score.

title: Qwen3-ASR
supportingClaims: Official source for the Qwen3-ASR model family and supported inference examples.

The repository lists English and Japanese for the 0.6B and 1.7B models; its streaming inference is currently available only through the vLLM backend and does not return timestamps, while timestamp output uses a separate forced aligner model.
The repository announced native Transformers support on 2026-06-26. Its model-name loading examples can download weights automatically.
limitations: The official repository does not document an Apple Silicon/Metal route for this app. Native Transformers support and the official vLLM streaming path do not establish an M1-compatible local implementation.

title: mlx-audio
supportingClaims: Community Apple Silicon runtime lead for speech models. Its current catalog lists Qwen3-ASR 0.6B 8-bit, Granite Speech, Nemotron, Whisper, MOSS Transcribe, and other STT routes, and links IBM Granite to an M-series example.
The repository states Apple Silicon M1/M2/M3/M4, Python 3.10+, and MLX requirements; this is runtime project documentation, not an app measurement.
limitations: Not Qwen/NVIDIA/IBM-authored or Apple-official; exact revisions, model conversions, supported operations, lifecycle, and this application's M1 result are unverified.

title: Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B
supportingClaims: Japanese ja-JP is listed as transcription-ready. The official card names a Q8_0 GGUF, gives a local NeMo-Speech.cpp route, and describes timestamps and confidence scores; governing terms are OpenMDW-1.1.
limitations: The card's quality metrics do not establish this application's Japanese Meet quality or M1 latency, memory, or backend behavior.

title: NeMo-Speech.cpp
supportingClaims: Current official docs list CPU, Metal, and Vulkan builds, a NeMo 3.5 local GGUF path, full/recorded-stream/microphone recognition, and stable C SDKs. The model conversion guide lists FP16 for Apple Silicon.
limitations: The runtime revision, actual Metal build, M1 model load, adapter lifecycle, and this app's memory/latency/quality remain unverified.

title: NeMo-Speech.cpp ASR configuration
supportingClaims: Language requests accept locale codes such as en-US and auto detection; the runtime documents a default 800 ms end-of-utterance silence threshold. Its gRPC adapter reports interim confidence as 0.0 and final RNNT confidence as 1.0, so that score is not a calibrated publication gate.
limitations: The docs do not establish app-specific JSON output mapping, Japanese score calibration, or a model-quality decision.

title: Qwen3.5-0.8B
supportingClaims: The card says 0.8B defaults to non-thinking and does not officially support Qwen3's /think and /no_think soft switches; its documented thinking control is an API chat-template parameter. The text-only path uses a user message.
limitations: That API parameter is not exposed by this repository's raw llama.cpp C API. The exact third-party GGUF tokenizer/template, EOS, and M1 result are still unverified.

title: Qwen3.5-2B
supportingClaims: The official card says 2B defaults to non-thinking; thinking control uses the documented chat-template/API option, not Qwen3 soft switches.
limitations: No artifact, quantization, exact tokenizer/template/EOS, license distribution review, or M1 run was selected or verified.

title: Qwen3.5-4B
supportingClaims: The official card says 4B defaults to thinking; thinking control uses the documented chat-template/API option, not Qwen3 soft switches. It gives non-thinking sampling guidance.
limitations: The raw llama.cpp C bridge cannot pass the chat-template option or all documented sampling controls. No artifact, exact template/EOS, license distribution review, or M1 run was verified.

title: Qwen3.5-9B
supportingClaims: The official card says 9B defaults to thinking and documents thinking control through chat-template/API settings rather than Qwen3 soft switches.
limitations: No artifact, quantization, exact tokenizer/template/EOS, license distribution review, or M1 run was selected or verified.

title: Hy-MT2
supportingClaims: The official project lists 1.8B GGUF artifacts, supports Japanese and English, recommends a target-language instruction with translation-only output, and states there is no default system prompt.
The current official README says the Hy-MT2 GGUF route depends on the STQ kernel released in llama.cpp PR #22836.
limitations: The linked GGUF artifact's exact provider/revision/hash, license terms for that converted artifact, required-kernel availability in this repository's pinned llama.cpp, EOS behavior, and M1 measurement remain unverified.

title: Hy-MT2-1.8B
supportingClaims: The card lists Apache-2.0 and includes target-language translation instructions, a terminology example, and says the models have no default system_prompt.
limitations: The current converted GGUF file/hash/terms, compatibility with this vendored llama.cpp and its special-token template, and M1 quality/performance remain unverified.

title: llama.cpp
supportingClaims: The local vendored source inspected for the current native translation bridge is this repository at the recorded commit.
limitations: The Makefile version label does not match the inspected vendor commit string; model-specific load, template, GGUF operators, and runtime lock still need a reproducible check.

title: TranslateGemma 4B IT
supportingClaims: Google's card supports 55 languages and a model-specific user content list with one text item containing only source text plus source_lang_code and target_lang_code; only User and Assistant roles are supported, and total input context is 2K.

The card states that the model files require review and acceptance of Google Gemma usage terms. The official technical report describes a 4B model fine-tuned from Gemma 3 using supervised and reinforcement-learning stages, not an explicit parameter-compression or knowledge-distillation method.
limitations: The official card and report provide no M1/Metal runtime result. No terms were accepted and no weights were retrieved. A generic Qwen prompt or unverified converted artifact cannot establish compatibility.

title: TranslateGemma announcement
supportingClaims: Google announced the TranslateGemma model family and intended translation use.
limitations: Announcement claims are not local quality or M1 performance measurements.

title: Riva-Translate-4B-Instruct-v2
supportingClaims: The card includes English/Japanese language pairs, model-specific prompt/template behavior, and usage terms.
limitations: Documentation examples use NVIDIA-oriented runtimes; M1 Metal, exact quantization, and local application integration are unverified.

title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2021) Technical Specifications
supportingClaims: Apple documents the 2021 16-inch MacBook Pro configurations and hardware specification.
limitations: Product specifications do not establish this application's measured performance.

owner: Apple machine learning research / MLX maintainers
title: MLX
supportingClaims: The project describes MLX as a machine-learning array framework for Apple silicon with Python, C++, C, and Swift APIs; its official documentation describes the CPU and GPU sharing unified memory.
limitations: Framework support and unified-memory design do not establish any particular ASR/translation model conversion, runtime adapter, M1 quality, or app integration.

title: A shared playbook for trustworthy third-party evaluations
supportingClaims: An evaluation report should identify the tested system and harness, task content, budgets, elicitation method, and validity checks so readers can tell what claim the result supports.
limitations: Frontier-safety evaluation guidance is a reporting/harness reference, not evidence about this application's ASR or translation quality.

title: Qwen3-8B
supportingClaims: The card documents enable_thinking, a default thinking-on mode, and the user soft switch /no_think. Its guidance says not to use greedy decoding in thinking mode and lists non-thinking sampling parameters.
limitations: The repository's C API cannot pass tokenizer chat-template kwargs or all listed sampling parameters; actual GGUF, model output, and local performance are unverified.

title: WebRTC VAD core
supportingClaims: The source implements frame-based VAD with 10 ms subframes and mode/frame-specific thresholds; it does not define a universal minimum utterance duration for a separate ASR product.
limitations: This repository uses its own energy VAD, not WebRTC VAD. The source does not calibrate the product's RMS thresholds or establish Japanese Meet quality or M1 performance.

title: whisper.cpp VAD speech segments
supportingClaims: The upstream example exposes a configurable minimum speech duration (250 ms in its current defaults), speech padding, and silence segmentation settings.
limitations: This repository does not use that example or its VAD model. Its defaults are not an application quality threshold and do not establish this app's M1 performance.

title: Message passing
supportingClaims: runtime.connect creates a named long-lived Port between extension contexts; the receiving extension service worker can handle it through runtime.onConnect and exchange messages over that Port.
limitations: Chrome documents Port routing and lifetime, not the application's complete privacy or session-recovery behavior. Browser integration still requires a manual extension/Meet trial.

title: Offscreen API
supportingClaims: An offscreen document is a hidden extension document and the runtime API is the only extension API available in that context; data/API access must use runtime messaging.
limitations: The source does not validate this application's audio graph, port reliability, or Meet behavior.

title: chrome.storage
supportingClaims: storage.session is in-memory, has a 10 MiB quota in current documentation, is cleared on extension/browser lifecycle events, and is restricted to trusted extension contexts by default.
limitations: The API provides temporary persistence, not a durable transcript archive; the app now caps the serialized caption state at 4 MiB, but application-level serialization and quota failure still require runtime verification.

title: From Text Metrics to Model Internals: A Study of Whisper ASR Hallucination Detection
supportingClaims: On human-annotated Whisper large-v3 data, text-based classifiers had high recall but degraded without reference transcripts; decoder-state probing performed best. This supports using uncalibrated text heuristics as review diagnostics rather than destructive publication decisions.
limitations: The result does not calibrate Whisper large-v3-turbo or another ASR backend for Japanese Meet audio, and decoder-state analysis is not implemented here.

title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
supportingClaims: The article reports that prompt, reference, and test defects can materially distort benchmark results and describes combined automated screening and human review; applied here only as a harness data-quality practice.
limitations: The study concerns coding benchmarks, not ASR or translation. It supplies no evidence about this application's model quality.

title: Granite 4.0 1B Speech
supportingClaims: IBM lists English and Japanese, ASR and bidirectional speech translation, and publishes an audio-marked transcription prompt with greedy Transformers generation settings. The model card also links an mlx-audio 0.4.1-or-later path and an 8-bit community artifact for Apple M-series.
limitations: The Apple path and quantized artifact are community runtime/conversion examples, not measured M1 execution. The model identifier says 1B while the hosted page metadata reports 2B parameters; artifact revision, actual parameter count, score semantics, streaming behavior, and application quality need verification.

title: MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B
supportingClaims: The card describes long-form transcription, diarization, timestamps, and acoustic event annotations; it requires custom Transformers code and shows a CUDA-oriented setup. The current card's competition description includes Japanese among 14 languages.
limitations: The card's language metadata and broader multilingual claims do not establish this application's Japanese quality. Its extra diarization output and custom remote code add integration work, and no official Apple Silicon path or M1 measurement was verified.

title: VibeVoice-ASR
supportingClaims: The model card labels the checkpoint as MIT-licensed and 51-language ASR/diarization and shows a Transformers load path; the hosted model repository is listed at roughly 17.3 GB.
limitations: The reviewed page did not establish a small quantized artifact or Apple Silicon/M1 execution path. Repository size and task labels are not application memory, latency, or quality measurements.

title: Hy-MT2-1.8B-1.25Bit-GGUF
supportingClaims: Tencent links this 1.25-bit AngelSlim GGUF artifact, lists Apache-2.0, and documents a local llama.cpp route. Its card says the format depends on the STQ kernel released in llama.cpp PR #22836.
limitations: The official repository gives a storage/speed claim but no numeric translation-quality score for this exact 1.25-bit variant in the reviewed report. Do not shortlist it until a relevant numerical score and a pinned compatible runtime are published.
File revision/hash, current STQ-kernel compatibility, template/EOS behavior, and M1 memory/latency remain unverified.

title: Hy-MT2-1.8B-GGUF
supportingClaims: The official author-linked GGUF repository lists the Q4_K_M variant and a local llama.cpp route, and displays Apache-2.0.
The current official repository lists Q4_K_M, Q6_K, and Q8_0 files and documents a local llama.cpp route.
limitations: The existing server registry pins a file URL revision, but its file hash and the exact compatibility with this repository's llama.cpp build were not tested.

title: FunASR AutoModel audio input contract
supportingClaims: The current AutoModel API accepts a one-dimensional NumPy waveform array (float32 at 16 kHz) and explicit sample-rate metadata, allowing decoded audio to be passed in memory.
limitations: This documents the Python input API only; it does not establish this repository's model output quality, M1 execution, or resource use.

title: WhisperX ASR input contract
supportingClaims: The current WhisperX transcribe method accepts either an audio file path or a NumPy waveform array.
limitations: This documents the Python input API only; it does not establish this repository's model output quality, M1 execution, or resource use.

title: Qwen3-ASR Technical Report
supportingClaims: The authors report a 0.6B accuracy-efficiency trade-off, a separate forced-alignment model, and Apache-2.0 release terms. These are author-reported findings.
limitations: Paper benchmarks and TTFT claims do not establish Japanese meeting quality, M1 behavior, application latency, memory, or the score/EOS semantics needed for publication.

title: Hy-MT2: A Family of Fast, Efficient and Powerful Multilingual Translation Models in the Wild
supportingClaims: The authors report the exact Hy-MT2-1.8B Q4_K_M quantized variant in Table 5: FLORES-200 82.22 versus BF16 83.49, and IFMTBench total 63.47 versus BF16 69.36. The corresponding relative retention is 98.48% and 91.51%.
The report describes the Hy-MT2-30B-A3B mixture-of-experts model and reports active-parameter naming separately from its 30B total parameter count.
limitations: These are author-reported results, including aggregate multilingual and translation-instruction metrics; they are not Japanese Meet holdout results and do not establish the exact artifact hash, this repository runtime compatibility, M1 memory/latency, or product quality.
The report provides no qualifying score for the linked AngelSlim 1.25-bit artifact. The 2-bit row retains only 85.05% of BF16 IFMTBench total, below the project's 90% secondary-metric screen.
The 30B-A3B total stored model is outside the 10 GiB inference-process peak budget even though only a subset of experts is active per token.

owner: Maryam Abbasihafshejani and Murtuza Jadliwala / arXiv
title: Reducing Hallucinated Transcripts in Whisper via Hallucination Space Projection
supportingClaims: The authors propose inference-time low-rank projection of Whisper decoder activations calibrated with non-speech data and report lower hallucination rates with a speech WER/false-rejection trade-off.
limitations: This is a paper-reported method, not a product validation. It requires decoder-internal access and its reported non-speech/speech benchmarks do not calibrate Whisper large-v3-turbo on Japanese Meet audio or establish M1 latency.

title: Qwen3.8-27B
supportingClaims: The reviewed official open checkpoint is a 27B dense causal language model with a vision encoder and thinking enabled by default; the card gives model parameter count as 27B.
limitations: The official page reviewed does not establish a <=4B Qwen3.8 checkpoint or a text-only path, and this model exceeds the project translation size and memory profile. Newer release status alone does not qualify it.

title: Whisper
supportingClaims: The official repository describes turbo as an optimized version of large-v3 with faster transcription and minimal accuracy degradation.
limitations: This does not establish accuracy on Japanese Meet audio, whisper.cpp behavior, M1 execution, or the application quality gate.

title: Kotoba-Whisper v2.2
supportingClaims: This is the author-published Kotoba-Whisper v2.2 checkpoint used as the current Kotoba comparison lead.
limitations: No M1 result or application-level Japanese meeting score was established by this review. A third-party conversion is a separate artifact and runtime.

title: Kotoba-Whisper-Bilingual v1.0
supportingClaims: The authors explicitly describe a distilled Whisper model with 0.8B hosted parameter metadata. The card gives Japanese ReazonSpeech held-out CER 16.8 versus 14.9 for Whisper large-v3; English scores are mixed by dataset.
The card provides model-specific language/task generation arguments, timestamps, and scores for ASR and speech-to-text translation.
limitations: On the Japanese ASR ReazonSpeech held-out test shown, the distilled model is worse than large-v3, so it fails the current benchmark-quality screen for replacing the bilingual Japanese ASR baseline. The card speed run used RTX 4090; it does not establish M1 performance.

The card also reports 756M parameter size in its inference table and 0.8B on hosted metadata; the exact safetensors/converted artifact, template/EOS, score semantics in this app, and M1 runtime remain unverified.

title: TranslateGemma Technical Report
supportingClaims: The report's WMT24++ table reports 4B TranslateGemma MetricX 5.32 and COMET22 80.1 versus Gemma 3 4B MetricX 6.97 and COMET22 77.2; lower MetricX and higher COMET22 are better. Its per-language English-to-Japanese MetricX is 4.44 versus 5.09 for Gemma 3 4B.

The 4B model is fine-tuned from the Gemma 3 4B checkpoint using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning; the paper does not describe this as a model-size compression or explicit knowledge-distillation variant.
limitations: The Japanese-to-English human MQM evaluation is reported for 27B and 12B models, not 4B. The report's 4B text score is one direction on WMT24++ and is not a Meet-specific bilingual holdout.
The weights require Gemma terms access; no terms were accepted, no artifact was downloaded, and no M1 runtime was verified.

title: CAT-Translate-1.4B
supportingClaims: The card reports Japanese-to-English / English-to-Japanese BLEU 33.26 / 34.19 and average bidirectional BLEU 33.73 on BSD, Court, JMed, PFMT, and WAT 2025 Patent subsets. It labels the artifact MIT, lists Japanese and English, and supplies the prompt "Translate the following {src_lang} text into {tgt_lang}.\n\n{src_text}" with the Sarashina 2.2 1B chat template.
Hosted metadata calls the checkpoint 1B parameters and BF16; the model ID/paper names it 1.4B.
limitations: The card describes LoRA as a training method for some training stages, not as a low-rank compressed inference artifact; do not classify the released model as low-rank factorization.

Published scores are author-reported on domain benchmarks, not this project's reviewed Meet corpus. Exact weight revision/hash, runtime/tokenizer/EOS adapter, memory, latency, and M1 performance remain unverified.

title: CAT-Translate: Building Compact Open-Source Models for Japanese-English Translation
supportingClaims: The paper reports a family of 0.8B, 1.4B, 3.3B, and 7B bilingual Japanese-English models and evaluates WMT plus real-world business, legal, medical, financial, and patent translation benchmarks.
limitations: The model-specific metrics and baselines were authored by the model developer; independent replication and local application performance are not established.

title: Gemma 4 E2B QAT Q4_0 GGUF
supportingClaims: The official repository describes a quantization-aware-trained Q4_0 GGUF Gemma 4 artifact and links the text/image/video multimodal model family.
limitations: The reviewed card did not provide relevant Japanese-English machine-translation quality scores for the exact quantized variant. It is not shortlisted under the published-benchmark screen; no M1 execution is claimed.

title: WMT26 Shared Task: Model Compression
supportingClaims: The task evaluates compact machine-translation systems with model artifacts and fixed hardware; its 2026 language pairs are Czech-German, English-Chinese, and English-Egyptian Arabic. It provides a primary-source precedent for judging both deployability and translation quality under a fixed protocol.
limitations: The 2026 task has no English-Japanese direction, so its results cannot qualify Japanese-English candidates for this project.

title: Shisa V2.1 LFM2 1.2B
supportingClaims: The authors describe a 1.2B Japanese-English general-purpose chat model and report Japanese MT-Bench 6.69 with GPT-4-Turbo, 6.13 with GPT-4o, 5.55 with GPT-4.1, and 4.19 with GPT-5.1.

The card says about 30% of the Shisa V2.1 core synthetic data was generated from Shisa V2 405B outputs; it does not describe the 1.2B model as a parameter-compressed or knowledge-distilled checkpoint.
The official card lists LFM1.0 license terms.
limitations: The reported Japanese MT-Bench aggregate does not provide separate Japanese-to-English and English-to-Japanese scores, so it does not meet the project bilingual compact-model screen.

The reported score uses an LLM judge and is not directly comparable to CAT BLEU or TranslateGemma MetricX. Exact local artifact, tokenizer/template, llama.cpp compatibility, and M1 behavior remain unverified.

title: Japanese MT-Bench harness
supportingClaims: The repository describes a reproducible Japanese MT-Bench harness and names GPT-4 Turbo as the standard judge used for comparison with older results.
limitations: This is an LLM-judged aggregate score and the reviewed materials do not identify separate JA-to-EN and EN-to-JA values for the Shisa 1.2B result.

title: Shisa V2.1 LFM2 1.2B GGUF
supportingClaims: The community repository publishes a GGUF conversion and documents a Q4_K_M llama.cpp command; its metadata reports LFM2 architecture and approximately 1B parameters.
limitations: This is not an author-provided conversion. Exact conversion provenance and hash, official license compatibility, the application chat template/EOS, llama.cpp pinned-build load, and M1 performance have not been verified.

owner: Pedram Rostami and Mohammad Javad Dousti / arXiv
title: CULL-MT: Compression Using Language and Layer pruning for Machine Translation
supportingClaims: The paper combines structural layer pruning with knowledge distillation and reports pruning 25% of NLLB-3.3B layers with a 0.9 spBLEU drop on Persian, French, and German to English.
limitations: The reported language directions are not Japanese-English. The paper does not qualify a small local bilingual model, a GGUF/MLX artifact, or an M1 runtime for this project.

title: JP-TL-Bench: Bidirectional Japanese-English Translation
supportingClaims: The authors define separate Japanese-to-English and English-to-Japanese sets and report model comparisons with a versioned anchor set using LLM pairwise judgments.
limitations: The published result set reviewed does not include a score for Shisa V2.1 LFM2 1.2B. The benchmark requires generated candidates and an LLM judge; it is not a local no-network product evaluation.

title: CAT-Translate-0.8B
supportingClaims: The card reports Japanese-to-English / English-to-Japanese BLEU 29.71 / 30.68 on BSD, Court, JMed, PFMT, and WAT 2025 Patent subsets; its table reports TranslateGemma 4B at 29.41 / 26.76 under the same evaluation.

The named artifact has 0.8B parameters and BF16 metadata, is MIT-licensed, and lists Japanese and English. The instruction is 'Translate the following {src_lang} text into {tgt_lang}.\n\n{src_text}' with the Sarashina 2.2 0.5B chat template and max_new_tokens=512.
limitations: These are model-author results on domain translation benchmarks, not the reviewed Meet corpus or an independent replication. Exact weights/tokenizer hashes, runtime/template/EOS behavior, M1 memory/latency, and application integration remain unverified.

title: Qwen3.8-27B-FP8
supportingClaims: The official card describes fine-grained FP8 quantization with block size 128 and says performance metrics are nearly identical to the original model; it identifies a 27B-parameter dense vision-language model.

The displayed benchmark table covers coding, agentic, instruction-following, reasoning, and vision-language tasks; it does not list Japanese-English machine-translation metrics. The card shows Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, and TokenSpeed routes.
limitations: The 'nearly identical' statement gives no exact Japanese-English score or comparable parent metric. At 27B FP8, the raw parameter weights alone are about 27 GB before scale data and runtime memory, above the project's 10 GiB inference-process peak. No Apple Silicon route or M1 result is established.

title: Explore large language models on Apple silicon with MLX
supportingClaims: Apple describes MLX as built for Apple silicon and its unified-memory architecture. The session demonstrates model use on an M3 Ultra with 512 GB unified memory.
limitations: Framework support and a much larger M3 Ultra demonstration do not establish this app's M1 Max model compatibility, quality, memory, or latency.

title: WMT24 Shared Task: General Machine Translation
supportingClaims: The task used unseen blind test paragraphs and human evaluation in document context; its specification distinguishes development and test data.
limitations: WMT24 is an external benchmark with its own domains, language directions, and protocol; it is not this project's reviewed Meet holdout or product-quality result.

title: WMT24++ dataset card
supportingClaims: The dataset schema retains document and segment identifiers, human post-edits, and a low-quality-source flag; its card recommends excluding flagged sources from evaluation.
limitations: No WMT24++ data was downloaded or added to the product evaluation set; public benchmark data does not replace human-reviewed meeting-domain development and holdout cases.

title: chrome.alarms API
supportingClaims: Chrome documents that alarms may be delayed an arbitrary amount beyond their scheduled time and that production alarms are limited to at most once every 30 seconds.
limitations: The API documentation does not establish the delay observed on a particular system or provide a service-level timing guarantee.

title: The extension service worker lifecycle
supportingClaims: Chrome documents that extension service workers normally terminate after 30 seconds of inactivity, that events or extension API calls reset the timer, and that global variables are lost when the worker shuts down.
limitations: The documented lifecycle does not measure this extension's timer scheduling or prove that an in-memory audio batch survives worker shutdown.

title: Migrate to a service worker
supportingClaims: Chrome documents that setTimeout and setInterval can be canceled when an extension service worker terminates, and recommends alarms for delayed operations that need to survive that termination.
limitations: This general guidance does not establish exact timing for a short one-shot flush scheduled during active audio processing; interruption can still lose volatile buffered audio.

title: Run local agentic AI on the Mac using MLX
supportingClaims: Apple describes MLX as an Apple-silicon array framework, MLX-LM as a model loading/quantization/fine-tuning layer, and MLX-LM Server as an OpenAI-compatible local HTTP server; the session discusses continuous batching and distributed inference.
limitations: The session's examples and performance discussion do not establish M1 Max quality, memory, latency, or compatibility for this extension. Adding MLX-LM Server as a second inference service would violate the current no-extra-relay constraint; replacing the existing service would require separate end-to-end integration evidence.

title: Meet Core AI
supportingClaims: Apple describes Core AI as an on-device framework spanning Apple silicon CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine, with Swift runtime APIs and Python/PyTorch conversion and optimization tooling; device-specific model specialization is part of deployment.
limitations: The session does not establish compatibility with the target M1 Max configuration, model-specific Japanese ASR/translation quality, this extension's Go loopback service, or end-to-end memory/latency. No runtime replacement is qualified.

title: Develop an extension for the Microsoft Edge sidebar
supportingClaims: Microsoft documents `chrome.sidePanel` for Edge extensions, the `sidePanel` manifest permission, `side_panel.default_path`, and opening the panel through `sidePanel.open()` after a user interaction.
limitations: API documentation does not prove this extension's behavior; the isolated Edge 154 M1 browser fixture supplies the implementation-specific check. Real Meet room behavior and store-distributed extension ID were not tested.

title: browser.tabCapture
supportingClaims: The tabCapture API can capture the current tab only after the user invokes the extension; a `targetTabId` is usable only when the extension has activeTab access. `getMediaStreamId()` can pass a stream to an offscreen document starting in Chrome 116.
limitations: The documentation does not establish Edge-version behavior or this application's audio quality/continuity; the Edge M1 fixture checks only its synthetic local tab.

title: The activeTab permission
supportingClaims: The activeTab permission grants temporary access to the current tab after an extension invocation, including action execution and a keyboard shortcut registered through the commands API.
limitations: This describes Chromium extension authorization, not an M1 model capability. The test-only shortcut is present only in the temporary extension copy, not the shipped manifest.

title: Cross-origin network requests
supportingClaims: An extension service worker or extension page can make cross-origin requests when its manifest grants the destination host permission; content scripts remain subject to the web origin's same-origin policy.
limitations: The documentation does not specify which Origin header Edge emits for this extension's loopback fetch. The run observed no Origin header; requests still require the local API bearer token.

title: Adapting your website for new Local Network Access restrictions in Microsoft Edge
supportingClaims: Microsoft says Edge's current Local Network Access restrictions do not apply to extensions with the necessary host permissions, or to local-to-loopback requests used by typical local development servers.
limitations: This browser policy documentation is time- and version-specific and does not remove the application's own bearer-token, loopback-bind, Host, or exact-Origin checks. It does not describe this extension's observed Origin header.

title: Host mapping rules
supportingClaims: Chromium host mapping rules support comma-separated `MAP` and `EXCLUDE` rules; a `MAP * ~NOTFOUND` rule can fail unmatched hostname resolution, while explicit exclusions remain resolvable.
limitations: The source describes Chromium resolver behavior, not Edge application UI. It is used only to isolate the disposable browser fixture; the script's loopback exception was verified by the M1 Edge API requests.

title: Launch Services
supportingClaims: Apple documents Launch Services as the macOS mechanism for opening or activating applications, similar to Finder or Dock.
limitations: This documentation does not establish why this Edge process crashed or guarantee that switching the harness to Launch Services will prevent another crash; only a safe retest can establish that.

title: CFBundleShortVersionString

limitations: Reading bundle metadata reports the installed bundle version; it does not prove that the same app instance launched or completed startup.
